summary: Sustained 5xx on embeddings route traced to ingress retry amplification and runtime overload
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (InkletAI) observed sustained elevated 5xx responses for /v1/embeddings starting 2026-03-13 09:12 UTC. Errors were concentrated on the embeddings ingestion route and coincided with a spike of small high-frequency requests from a single tenant.

Impact:
- ~15% error rate on embeddings API for InkletAI for ~2 hours during peak (customers reported failures and retries).
- Increased latency and token cost due to hedged retries stacking.
- Internal alerts: api-gateway 5xx rate, serving-runtime worker restarts, autoscaler scaling loops.

Environment:
- prod, us-east region, dedicated routing for enterprise tenants.
- Affected service: embeddings ingestion fronted by api-gateway -> ingress-prioritizer -> embeddings-service running open-embedder-v2 quant variant.

Steps to reproduce (investigator steps):
1) Replay a small-payload high-QPS traffic pattern (1000 qps sustained) to /v1/embeddings with short keepalive.
2) Observe gateway queue growth and upstream 502/504s as hedged retries are triggered.
3) Watch serving-runtime create additional lightweight worker processes which then hit GPU kernel contention and throttle.

Observed behavior:
- api-gateway returned a mixture of 502/503/504 with a very short tail of 500s.
- Metrics show gateway retransmit (hedged retries) multiplier increasing request fanout to upstream by ~2.7x at peak.
- Serving runtime showed CPU spin and frequent worker restarts (OOM was not observed; GPU kernel timeouts increased).

Expected behavior:
- Gateway should shed and queue gracefully, hedged retries should be bounded to avoid amplifying upstream load.
- Serving runtime should maintain stable worker count under backpressure and defer to autoscaler when capacity is needed.

Initial mitigation applied:
- Temporarily reduced hedged-retry window on the api-gateway for embeddings route (control plane change at 2026-03-13 09:37 UTC).
- Applied a soft rate limit per-tenant to limit immediate burst from the InkletAI tenant at 09:45 UTC.
- Throttled inbound keepalive churn by increasing server-side keepalive idle timeout to reduce ephemeral connection churn.

Current ask:
- Root cause analysis and permanent fix to avoid retry amplification and to make serving-runtime resilient to short high-frequency tenant bursts.

investigation_notes:
Findings summary:
- The immediate trigger was a high-frequency small-payload burst from a single tenant which interacted poorly with current hedged-retry settings.
- Hedged retries were configured with a short-delay aggressive policy on embeddings route to optimize tail latency; under load this multiplied upstream requests ~2.7x and pushed serving-runtime into a hot-loop trying to satisfy fanout.
- Serving runtime showed long kernel queues on the embedding model variant; not OOMs but scheduling contention and repeated kernel preemption causing elevated latency and runtime worker churn.
- Autoscaler oscillation: rapid worker spin-ups followed by backoff created resource thrash and made recovery slower.
Evidence and logs:
- Dashboard: https://metrics.redwood.com/d/embeddings/replica-health?orgId=1&from=now-3h&to=now (auth required).
- Gateway trace sample: link to trace id apigw-trace-20260313-0912-77 (in internal tracing).
- Heap/worker logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/us-east/embeddings/2026-03-13/worker-churn.log
Related artifacts:
- Slack thread: #support-embeddings (thread ts 1678764000.000200)
resolution:
Short-term fixes completed:
- Hedge retry window reduced and retry cap enforced per-route to prevent amplification (rolled at 2026-03-13 09:37 UTC).
- Tenant soft-rate-limit applied for InkletAI to allow customer traffic to drain without overwhelming upstream while we patch the platform.
- Increased keepalive idle timeout to reduce ephemeral connection churn.

Long-term actions (owner assigned):
1) PLAT-5238 (Luis Ortega) - Add exponential backoff + per-route hedged-retry cap to api-gateway. Target: 2026-03-20.
2) PLAT-5243 (Nora Singh) - Add admission-control debounce in ingress-prioritizer to detect tenant micro-bursts and apply local shedding. Target: 2026-03-27.
3) RUN-3301 (SRE) - Tune autoscaler to use stabilized scaling window for embeddings workers to avoid thrash. Target: 2026-03-22.
4) Postmortem and customer write-up (Support): prepare by 2026-03-18 and share with InkletAI and internal stakeholders.

Resolution notes for customer:
- We applied mitigations which significantly reduced observed failures; platform patch PRs are in review. We'll follow up with a detailed postmortem and recommended client-side best practices for bursty traffic (client-side rate limiting and jittered retries).
